title: Brent Interview — The Role, the Programme, the Room
description: Broadview International Trainee Programme, Finance Track, final round 25 Aug 2026. What the programme is, what Finance does at Broadview, how the selection really works, who is likely in the room, and how to frame 'why Broadview'. Study-only two-part cards (what they want to hear + my angle).

cards.front: Describe the International Trainee Programme in 20 seconds.
cards.general: 18-month fixed-term contract; two or three projects in different group companies and countries; six tracks (Finance, Business Analytics, Technology & Innovation, Manufacturing, Sustainability, Legal) plus a Mixed Track; four two-day training sessions in the Netherlands; housing and flights provided when relocated; intended permanent group role afterwards for strong performers.
cards.specific: What attracts me is the shape of it: real projects with senior-management attention from day one, relocation between operating companies, and finance that sits next to factories and CEOs rather than in a reporting silo. That is exactly the combination I have been looking for to start my career.
cards.hint: 18 months · 2–3 projects · 6 tracks + Mixed · 4×2-day trainings · relocation.

cards.front: What does Broadview say the Finance Track is for?
cards.general: In Broadview's own words: 'convert sales growth into higher profits and cash'. Plus: monitor financial performance, identify improvement opportunities, safeguard reporting compliance, improve internal controls and financial reporting. Published example projects: factory control via mass balances at Arpa (Bra) and a reporting tool aligned to the Broadview Business System at Formica Europe.
cards.specific: I quote that phrase back: 'converting sales into profit and cash'. It is what I found most interesting at Philips — not producing the KPI, but understanding what moved it and what that meant commercially — and it is what Broadview's 2025 numbers are about.
cards.hint: 'Convert sales growth into higher profits and cash.'

cards.front: What does a Broadview Business Controller actually do (from the vacancy)?
cards.general: Coordinates monthly reporting, quarterly forecasts and annual budgets; evaluates strategy effectiveness; works closely with local CFOs; challenges company leadership using in-depth analyses across the full P&L, market and production; business-intelligence affinity; travel up to ~50% during peaks.
cards.specific: This is the role I am aiming at after the programme. The word that matters is 'challenge': finance at Broadview is expected to push back on management with facts. That suits me — at TheFork my project was precisely diagnosing a problem and persuading senior managers in several countries to act on it.
cards.hint: Reporting + forecast + budget; challenge leadership with P&L + market + production.

cards.front: What is the official four-step selection process?
cards.general: 1. CV screening (academic results, international experience, affinity). 2. Video interview ('to get to know you'). 3. Online analytical assessment. 4. Final round: face-to-face with senior management at one of the offices — 'this involves a business case'.
cards.specific: I am at step 4. Candidates report a take-home 'investment case' prepared over about a week, presented in person (~1 hour) and then defended — 'very difficult, requires proper preparation'. So I prepare a case presentation with numbers, not a conversation.
cards.hint: CV → video → online test → final round with senior management + business case.

cards.front: What do candidates report about the final round?
cards.general: A ~30-minute HR call on motivation and fit with Broadview values ('very important to them'); an online numerical/analytical test; then an investment case prepared in roughly a week and presented at head office, followed by questioning. Reported questions: motivation, where in 5 years, strengths vs the requirements, how you work in a team, your biggest failure.
cards.specific: My prep order: case deliverable first, then the four personal stories, then the numbers. Presentation: conclusion on slide one, one table of numbers, one risk slide, ten minutes, then take questions without bluffing.
cards.hint: Take-home investment case → present ~1 hour → defend. Questions: motivation, 5 years, failure.

cards.front: Who runs the programme and what do they look for?
cards.general: Klaasje Huijbregts, Talent Development Manager — recruits trainees and ensures 'diverse and challenging projects'; says trainees 'work closely with the CEOs and senior management from day one'. Elsje Ouwehand, Capabilities Director — values 'mental strength', the ability to 'deal with ambiguity and change', and 'humbleness, transparency and open communication'.
cards.specific: Those words map onto my stories: ambiguity and change = Tekkers and the China exchange; humbleness and transparency = the feedback story about too much detail and the Tekkers disagreement where I changed my view on evidence.
cards.hint: Huijbregts (talent), Ouwehand (capabilities): mental strength, ambiguity, humbleness, transparency.

cards.front: Who is Broadview's CEO, and what should you know about the board?
cards.general: Matthijs (M.J.) Schoten is CEO and the sole named Executive Board member; from 1 Jan 2026 he also chairs Westag's management board. Supervisory Board: M.F.J.P. Vrijsen (chair), A.E. ter Laak, J.C. Hoogerbrugge, W.M.J. Pijbes, M.P.M. Roef. A CFO (Hielke Sybesma) appears in business databases but not on the website — treat as probable.
cards.specific: If Schoten or the CFO is in the room I expect short, direct, numerical challenge. My rule: answer the question asked, give the number, stop. If I don't know, say so and say how I would find out.
cards.hint: CEO Matthijs Schoten (also Westag chair 2026); SB chair Vrijsen.

cards.front: What are Broadview's stated values and culture cues?
cards.general: Values page: 'Company first'; openness and honesty; 'political behaviour is not appreciated'; long-term orientation. A Glassdoor review of the programme (4/5) praises learning from high-level managers but calls the HQ finance culture 'macho'.
cards.specific: Translation for me: be direct, be factual, never posture. Composure under pushback is part of the test, so when a number is challenged I acknowledge, state the assumption, give the sensitivity, and either hold or explicitly change the conclusion.
cards.hint: Company first · openness · no politics · expect direct pushback.

cards.front: What candidate profile does Broadview publish?
cards.general: Master's degree with 'excellent grades'; full command of English, other European languages an asset; previous experience of living abroad 'indicates that you will be able to adjust'; EU work permit preferred; Finance Track targets Finance, Accounting & Control, Financial Management graduates. Recruiting runs year-round; cohorts have started in September. 'Competitive salary', housing and flights when relocated, mentoring from the HR director.
cards.specific: I tick the boxes explicitly: MSc Financial Management (Corporate Finance), Dutch/EU, 7+ years abroad across Switzerland, Italy, China and the US. Languages: I state my real levels — Italian after a year in Rome and any German from Switzerland matter for Bra and Westag rotations.
cards.hint: Master's, excellent grades, English + other languages, lived abroad, EU permit.

cards.front: Where could a Finance trainee realistically be sent?
cards.general: Evidenced by past finance projects: Den Bosch (HQ), Bra in Italy (Arpa), Newcastle / North Shields (Formica Europe), Germany (Westag), Cincinnati (Formica North America). Other programme locations across tracks: Paris, New York, Rotterdam, Weert, Istanbul, Shanghai, Singapore. Projects follow live business needs, not preferences.
cards.specific: I say I am fully mobile for the 18 months and mean it. I do not shop for locations in the interview; I ask what problems are live, not which cities.
cards.hint: Den Bosch, Bra, Newcastle, Germany, Cincinnati. Don't shop for cities.

cards.front: Name three published Finance Track trainee projects and what each tells you.
cards.general: Giacomo Ugolini: data quality of the group reporting tool (Den Bosch); Formica Europe reports aligned to the Broadview Business System plus price analyses (Newcastle); Arpa factory control with mass balances (Bra) — now Business Analyst, Formica Europe; key learning 'the helicopter view'. Asia Pawluch: reporting-tool implementation, then Westag reporting automation — now Financial Controller at HQ; 'immediately put in a position with a lot of responsibility'. Kavya Movva: US post-acquisition synergies and scrap-reporting harmonisation across US/Italy/UK.
cards.specific: Pattern: reporting quality → commercial analysis → factory KPIs. That is the ladder I want to climb, and the mass-balance work at Bra is the single project I would most like, because it puts finance on the factory floor.
cards.hint: Giacomo (tool → Formica EU → Arpa mass balance); Asia (tool → Westag → Controller); Kavya (synergies, scrap).

cards.front: Which alumni are now senior at Broadview, and why mention it?
cards.general: Alessandra Fusi — Chief Sustainability Officer; Arnout Hamster — CEO Broadview Energy Solutions; Stefano Mion — CEO Arpa; Marc Corbeij — Commercial Excellence Director; Pieter Peters — Director Group R&D (Nemho). Recent alumni: Financial Controller at HQ, Business Analysts at Formica Europe and Musa, BI Specialist at HQ.
cards.specific: It tells me the programme is a genuine leadership pipeline, which answers 'where do you see yourself in five years': a business controller in an operating company, having owned at least one factory-finance project, on the path those alumni took.
cards.hint: Fusi (CSO), Hamster (CEO Energy), Mion (CEO Arpa) — real pipeline.

cards.general: Pick reasons specific to the company, each tied to something the candidate has actually done: (1) the kind of finance it practises, (2) the programme's structure, (3) the industry.
cards.specific: One: finance that converts sales into profit and cash, next to factories and CEOs — what I enjoyed at Philips and TheFork, done properly. Two: 18 months, 2–3 projects, relocation — I have lived in four countries and I learn fastest when thrown in. Three: materials and energy are essential, physical industries with many moving parts; ProtecShin gave me a real taste of a product where the material *was* the value proposition.
cards.hint: Finance next to the business · relocation fits me · materials are tangible (ProtecShin).

cards.front: How do you mention openness to Business Analytics without sounding undecided?
cards.general: Anchor first, flexibility second. Interviewers penalise candidates who seem to be hedging between tracks; they reward those who know what they want and are pragmatic about project allocation.
cards.specific: 'Finance is my anchor — I like understanding what drives performance and turning that into decisions. What attracts me to Broadview is that finance is connected to operations, markets and strategy, so I would welcome a mixed project, especially Business Analytics, if it strengthens that finance path. I am not applying because I am undecided.'
cards.hint: Finance is the anchor; BA welcome only if it strengthens the finance path.

cards.front: Where do you see yourself in five years?
cards.general: Answer with a role that exists inside the company and a capability you will have built, not a title ladder. Show you understand the programme's intended outcome: a permanent group role.
cards.specific: Business controller in one of the operating companies — ideally having owned a factory-finance project like the Bra mass-balance work and a group-level reporting or Broadview One synergy project — with a reputation for analysis that turns into action. Longer term, the CFO-type path the programme is designed to feed.
cards.hint: Business controller in an OpCo; owned a factory-finance project; analysis → action.
